designSummary: Single-arm feasibility study; estimation of recruitment, delivery and completeness rates against progression criteria.
sampleSize: About 112 eligible patients are expected in nine months. With 112 eligible patients, a recruitment rate near 50 percent is estimated within about 9 percentage points (95 percent confidence). With about 56 recruited patients, delivery and completeness rates near 85 to 90 percent are estimated within about 8 to 9 points. This is enough to judge the progression criteria, not to estimate an effect.
primaryAnalysis: Recruitment rate with a 95 percent confidence interval, compared with the 50 percent criterion; a traffic-light rule (proceed, amend, stop) fixed in advance.
secondaryAnalysis: Delivery and completeness rates against their criteria; proportion with glucose out of range and its interval to inform a trial sample size; questionnaire scores.
missingData: Missing glucose values are the completeness outcome itself and are reported, not imputed.
multiplicity: No hypothesis tests; three criteria judged by pre-specified rules.
overfittingGuards: No effect estimate reported as efficacy
summary: Precision adequate to judge three progression criteria.
